question.text: Consider the Poisson distribution $\textrm{Po}(11).$ Rounding to $4$ decimal digits, fill in the missing value in the corresponding table for the cumulative distribution function below.
question.freeAnswerChoice:
$ \quad x \quad $ $6$ $7$ $8$ $9$ $10$ $11$ $12$
$ P(X\leq x) $ $\,0.0786\,$ $\,0.1432\,$ $\,0.2320\,$ $\,0.3405\,$ [answer: 0.4599; type: number; width: 50; margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0;] $\,0.5793\,$ $\,0.6887\,$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

The probability mass function for the Poisson distribution $\textrm{Po}(\lambda)$ is given by \[ f(x) = \dfrac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x!}, \qquad x=0,1,2,3, \ldots\,. \]

In our case, $\lambda=11.$

Therefore, we compute the missing element of the table as follows:

\begin{align*} F(10) &= P(X \leq 10) \\[5pt] &= P(X \leq 9) + P(X=10) \\[5pt] &= F(9) + P(X=10) \\[5pt] &= 0.3405 + \dfrac{11^{10} \cdot e^{-11}}{10!} \\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.4599} \end{align*}

question.text:
Using the cumulative distribution function table of the Poisson random variable $X \sim \textrm{Po}(15)$ given below, compute $P(X=9).$

$ \quad x \quad $ $5$ $6$ $7$ $8$ $9$ $10$ $11$
$ P(X\leq x) $ $\,0.0028\,$ $\,0.0076\,$ $\,0.0180\,$ $\,0.0374\,$ $\,0.0699\,$ $\,0.1185\,$ $\,0.1848\,$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} F(9) &= P(X \leq 9) \\[5pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,\ldots,9 \}) \\[5pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,\ldots,8 \}) + P(X= 9) \\[5pt] &= P(X \leq 8) + P(X=9) \\[5pt] &= F(8) + P(X=9). \end{align*} \]

Therefore,

\[ \begin{align*} P(X=9) &= F(9) - F(8) \\[3pt] &= 0.0699- 0.0374 \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.0325}. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing a Poisson Probability Using a CDF Table

question.text:
Using the cumulative distribution function table of the Poisson random variable $X \sim \textrm{Po}(9)$ given below, compute $P(4 \leq X \leq 7).$

$ \quad x \quad $ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$ $6$ $7$ $8$
$ P(X\leq x) $ $\,0.0062\,$ $\,0.0212\,$ $\,0.0550\,$ $\,0.1157\,$ $\,0.2068\,$ $\,0.3239\,$ $\,0.4557\,$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} F(7) &= P(X \leq 7) \\[3pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,\ldots,7\}) \\[3pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,2,3\}) + P(X \in \{ 4,5,6,7\}) \\[3pt] &= P(X \leq 3) + P(4 \leq X \leq 7) \\[3pt] &= F(3) + P(4 \leq X \leq 7). \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} P(4 \leq X \leq 7) &= F(7) - F(3) \\[3pt] &= 0.3239 - 0.0212 \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.3027}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing a Poisson Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF Table

question.text:
Using the cumulative distribution function table of the Poisson random variable $X \sim \textrm{Po}(5)$ given below, compute $P(2 \lt X \lt 4).$

$ \quad x \quad $ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$ $6$
$ P(X\leq x) $ $\,0.0067\,$ $\,0.0404\,$ $\,0.1247\,$ $\,0.2650\,$ $\,0.4405\,$ $\,0.6160\,$ $\,0.7622\,$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} F(3) &= P(X \lt 4) \\[3pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,2,3 \}) \\[3pt] &= P(X \in \{ 0,1,2 \}) + P(X \in \{ 3 \}) \\[3pt] &= P(X \leq 2) + P(2 \lt X \lt 4) \\[3pt] &= F(2) + P(2 \lt X \lt 4). \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} P(2 \lt X \lt 4) &= F(3) - F(2) \\[3pt] &= 0.2650 - 0.1247\\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.1403}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing a Poisson Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF Table

question.text:
Using the cumulative distribution function table of the Poisson random variable $X \sim \textrm{Po}(4.5)$ given below, compute $P(X \geq 6).$

$ \quad x \quad $ $3$ $4$ $5$ $6$ $7$ $8$ $9$
$ P(X\leq x) $ $\,0.3423\,$ $\,0.5321\,$ $\,0.7029\,$ $\,0.8311\,$ $\,0.9134\,$ $\,0.9597\,$ $\,0.9829\,$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

\[ P(X > a) = 1 - P(X\leq a) = 1-F(a). \]

Now, note that

\[ P(X \geq 6) = P(X \gt 5). \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} P(X \geq 6) &= P(X \gt 5) \\[5pt] &= 1 - P(X\leq 5) \\[5pt] &= 1 - F(5) \\[5pt] &= 1 - 0.7029\\[5pt] &= 0.2971. \end{align*}
